about: What a law firm or accountancy practice may change in the Halden & Vale design. Protected: the scroll-run matter on the desk (a first note, papers arriving, sorted into tabbed folders, a close read with highlights and flags, the advice memo typed out, signed and stamped), the what-do-you-need guide, the fee cards and VAT switch, the people cards, the first-call booking, layout, type and all interaction code. The firm's own words, areas and situations, fees, people, promises, regulator line and the example matter come from the content.
rules: Text may not contain < > { } or line breaks.

stages: the six steps of one example matter the hero works, in order: first contact, papers arrive, sorted, the close read (points flagged), the advice, the result. Each has a short name, a caption and the day count since the matter opened (rising).

matter: the example's reference, how many points the close read flags (1-3), its fixed fee as shown, the word stamped at the end, the 3-5 folder labels the papers are sorted under, and the advice memo's title and 2-4 short points.

guide.areas: two to five areas of work, each with one to four situations a client might be in: a fee range [low, high], how long it takes, who handles it (a name in people.list), two to four steps and what to have ready.
fees.items: one to four headline fixed fees (from: true when it is a starting price) with what's included. fees.vat is the VAT rate in percent (0 hides the VAT switch).
consult.how: in this order, the ways of meeting offered: phone, video, in person (the first one to three). consult.slots: the times offered on weekdays (H:MM, 24-hour).
